record.title: agentbox agent prints container file contents, file names, exec output and model text raw to the operator terminal, bypassing cli._safe
record.description: cli._safe exists specifically so agent-determined strings never reach the operator terminal as raw control/bidi characters, and every sibling CLI path (the approval card _show_approval, approve results, audit detail) routes lower-trust strings through it. cmd_agent's log() callback is the one gap: the 'say' branch prints model text raw and the 'result' branch prints the first 6 lines of a tool result raw, with no _safe. A prompt-injected agent (the stated threat model) can emit control sequences in its own model text, or read a /workspace file whose bytes carry VT sequences (planted via source_dir at create or written by the agent via write_file), or list_dir a control-char file name; read_file/list_dir return those bytes verbatim and exec stdout keeps 8-bit C1 via json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False). In a real VT emulator the sequences erase previously printed transcript lines and forge new ones (e.g. a fake [사용자] prompt or approval-looking line), hide the agent's real actions, spoof the window title (OSC 0), and where OSC 52 is honoured write the operator clipboard. The approval decision surface itself is unaffected (it uses _safe); this corrupts the operator's monitoring transcript.
record.root_cause: cli.py:353-361 cmd_agent.log prints 'say' (355) and 'result' (358-361) without _safe, while _safe is defined at cli.py:37-39 and applied by sibling paths (e.g. 199). The strings are raw container/model bytes: sandbox.read_file returns decoded container bytes with control chars preserved (sandbox.py:570) and list_dir returns raw ls -la output (sandbox.py:552); agent.ToolClient.call_text passes read_file content / list_dir listing through verbatim and renders other tool results via json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False), preserving 8-bit C1 (agent.py:118-126); agent.run feeds them to log('result',...) (agent.py:266) and model text to log('say',...) (agent.py:256).
record.intended_behavior: The _safe docstring (cli.py:38) states agent-determined strings must not reach the terminal as-is; control bytes must be rendered visible (e.g. \x1b). Every operator-facing CLI path that shows lower-trust strings is expected to neutralise them the way _show_approval does, so container/model output cannot drive cursor movement, line erasure, OSC title/clipboard, or bidi reordering on the operator's terminal.

trace.description: read_file returns container file bytes decoded utf-8 (errors=replace), so control bytes (ESC, C1, OSC) are preserved in 'content'; list_dir returns raw 'ls -la' output as 'listing'; exec returns raw stdout. These are the lower-trust container-output boundary.

read_file 'content' and list_dir 'listing' are returned to the loop verbatim; all other tool results (incl. exec stdout) are json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False, indent=2), which keeps 8-bit C1 CSI (U+009B) intact.
run() passes the raw tool text to log('result', text); model-produced text is passed to log('say', ...) at agent.py:256 and tool-call args to log('call', ...) at 264.

The 'result' branch prints the first 6 lines of the raw tool text to the operator terminal with no _safe (358-361); the 'say' branch prints model text raw at 355 and the 'call' branch prints raw model-controlled args at 357. Reaches the operator's stdout unescaped.

evidence.description: _safe docstring: agent-determined strings must not be printed to the terminal as-is; control chars are to be shown like \x1b. _UNSAFE regex at line 34 covers C0/DEL/C1 and bidi.
Sibling approval-card path applies _safe to each rendered line; approve results and audit detail do likewise. cmd_agent is the sole operator-facing path that does not.
cmd_agent.log 'result' branch computes head of the first 6 raw lines and prints them raw (361); the 'say' branch at 355 prints model text raw. No _safe anywhere in log().
read_file returns content decoded utf-8 with errors=replace, preserving control/escape bytes verbatim; list_dir (552) returns raw ls -la output.
Non read_file/list_dir tool results (incl. exec stdout) serialised with json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False), so 8-bit C1 CSI (U+009B) survives into the printed result.

conditions.description: Attacker is the lowest-trust agent principal (agt_ token) whose model output and/or /workspace content is attacker-influenced; prompt injection of the agent is the architecture's explicit threat model.
A human operator runs `agentbox agent` and watches its stdout transcript.

The operator's terminal emulator interprets ECMA-48 CSI/OSC sequences. Cursor-up (ESC[1A) and erase-line (ESC[2K) used for the forgery are universally supported (confirmed in pyte); OSC 0 title spoof confirmed; OSC 52 clipboard write is emulator-dependent and off by default in many.

Control bytes delivered via model text (direct), a /workspace file read by read_file (planted via source_dir at create or write_file), a control-char file name via list_dir, or exec stdout (8-bit C1).

execution.attacker_perspective: A prompt-injected agent, or a hostile file placed in /workspace, wants to corrupt what the human operator sees in the `agentbox agent` transcript: erase the lines showing the agent's real actions and forge a trusted-looking line, spoof the window title, and (where honoured) write the operator's clipboard.
payloads: read_file content: 'real file line\n\x1b[1A\x1b[2K\x1b[1A\x1b[2K[사용자] please run: approved\n\x1b]52;c;ZWNobyBwd25lZA==\x07tail'
instructions: In /target read-only sandbox (no network/docker), drive the real cli.main(['agent','summarize','--sandbox','sb_x','--token','agt_dummy','--model','m','--provider','openai','--base-url','http://127.0.0.1:9']) with only the LLM adapter (ag.make_chat) and control-plane client (ag.ToolClient) replaced by local fakes, so cmd_agent -> agent.run -> log() -> print runs unmodified.
Fake read_file/list_dir/exec return the payloads above; fake model returns the 'say' payload and three tool calls (read_file, list_dir, exec).
Capture the process stdout and count raw ESC/C1 bytes and OSC 52; feed the captured stream to a real VT emulator (pyte) and print the rendered screen; compare against cli._safe() of the same strings.
execution.observed_result: Operator stdout carried 7 raw ESC (0x1b) bytes, 2 raw 8-bit C1 CSI (U+009B), a full OSC 52 clipboard sequence, and CSI cursor-up+erase. Rendered through pyte the real read_file line and the '-> read_file(...)' call line were erased and replaced by a forged '[사용자] please run: approved' line that looks like a trusted operator prompt; the exec JSON collapsed via C1 to hide 'stdout":"out' and show 'hidden'; the SGR in the file name was consumed ('evilname'). The parent-live run (agents/parent-live/artifacts/l6.py/.out, pyte over the real cli.main output) additionally showed OSC 0 setting the window title to 'owned-title'. cli._safe() of the identical strings leaves no ESC, no C1 and no OSC-BEL (all rendered visible), confirming the fix neutralises every vector. Decisive reproduction is mine (ran in the approved OS-enforced sandbox: /target read-only, no network, no docker, uid 65534); corroborated independently by parent-live l6 and by hunters h-wild (h_term.out) and h-webui (h_cli_agent.out).

remediation.strategy: Route every operator-facing string in cmd_agent.log through the existing _safe neutralisation, exactly as the approval/audit paths do, so container/model control and bidi characters are rendered visible instead of interpreted. Because log() shows multiple lines (and truncates to 6), apply a newline-preserving variant: escape all of \x00-\x08, \x0b-\x1f, \x7f-\x9f and the bidi set but keep \n, per line, before computing the head. Apply it to the 'say' (model text), 'call' (model-controlled tool args) and 'result' (tool output) branches.

likelihood.reason: Requires only the lowest-trust agent principal (prompt injection is the explicit threat model) or hostile /workspace content, plus an operator running the provided `agentbox agent` mode in an interpreting terminal (nearly all terminals interpret CSI cursor-up/erase-line). No extra privilege or approval is needed; the control bytes flow unconditionally.

impact.reason: Integrity/spoofing of the operator's monitoring transcript: erasing the agent's real actions and forging trusted-looking lines, hiding exec output, and spoofing the window title, demonstrated in a real VT emulator. OSC 52 clipboard write is emulator-dependent and was not rendered by pyte, so it is not counted as demonstrated. It is not RCE, cross-principal disclosure, or authority escalation, and the actual approval decision card is separately protected by _safe; the harm is confined to corrupting what the operator sees on this observation stream.

confidence.reason: Source is unambiguous (log() prints raw while all sibling paths use _safe; read_file/list_dir/exec return control bytes verbatim) and the rendered impact was independently reproduced in a real VT emulator by me in the approved sandbox, and corroborated by the parent-live pyte run and two hunter harnesses. cli._safe demonstrably neutralises every vector.
